films.title: Tremors
films.writers: S. S. Wilson and Brent Maddock (story by Wilson, Maddock, Ron Underwood)
films.villain: Graboids - giant subterranean worms that hunt by sensing vibrations; tentacle 'tongues'; named by store owner Walter Chang
notes: Reba McEntire's acting debut
Ron Underwood's feature directorial debut
Working title 'Land Sharks' (dropped due to SNL's Land Shark); script title 'Beneath Perfection'
Spawned 6 direct-to-video sequels starting with Tremors 2: Aftershocks (1996) and a 2003 TV series
Filmed in Inyo County, California (Lone Pine / Alabama Hills); released Jan 19, 1990

films.title: Misery
films.basedOn: Misery (1987 novel) by Stephen King
films.setting: Annie Wilkes's remote home near Silver Creek, Colorado
films.villain: Annie Wilkes (Kathy Bates), a nurse and Paul's self-proclaimed 'number one fan'
notes: Kathy Bates won the Best Actress Oscar - only film based on a Stephen King novel to win an Oscar
'Hobbling' scene: Annie breaks Paul's ankles with a sledgehammer (in the novel she severs a foot with an ax)
Paul writes Victorian romance novels about Misery Chastain
Annie Wilkes ranked #17 on AFI's 100 Heroes & Villains
Opened #2 behind Home Alone; Bates also won the Golden Globe (Drama)

films.title: Jacob's Ladder
films.setting: Brooklyn, New York City (1975) and Vietnam's Mekong Delta (1971)
films.villain: Demonic hallucinations; Army drug 'the Ladder' secretly given to Jacob's unit
notes: Twist: Jacob is dying in a Vietnam triage tent; the 1975 life is in his mind
Writer Bruce Joel Rubin also wrote Ghost (1990)
Major inspiration for the Silent Hill games (incl. head-shaking effect)
Head-shaking effect: actors shot at low frame rate
Remade in 2019

films.title: Arachnophobia
films.writers: Don Jakoby and Wesley Strick (story by Don Jakoby and Al Williams)
films.setting: Canaima, California (fictional; filmed in Cambria, CA); opens in Venezuela
films.villain: Deadly Venezuelan spider 'the General' and its hybrid offspring; the General was a Goliath birdeater nicknamed 'Big Bob'
notes: Frank Marshall's directorial debut; Spielberg and Marshall executive producers
First film released by Disney's Hollywood Pictures
Delbert McClintock (John Goodman) is the exterminator
Over 300 New Zealand Avondale spiders used
Won Saturn Award for Best Horror Film; Jeff Daniels won Saturn Best Actor

films.title: It
films.yearNote: Aired on ABC Nov 18 and 20, 1990
films.writers: Lawrence D. Cohen and Tommy Lee Wallace (teleplay)
films.basedOn: It (1986 novel) by Stephen King
films.villain: It - shapeshifter mostly appearing as Pennywise the Dancing Clown (Tim Curry); true form a giant spider
notes: Seth Green played young Richie; Emily Perkins young Beverly; Olivia Hussey played Bill's wife Audra
George A. Romero was first set to direct but left over the NOTLD remake
Filmed in Vancouver on a $12M budget; nearly 30M viewers, ABC's biggest 1990 success
Richard Bellis won an Emmy for the score
Georgie is killed at a storm drain chasing his paper boat

films.title: The Exorcist III
films.basedOn: Legion (1983 novel) by William Peter Blatty
films.villain: The Gemini Killer (James Venamun, Brad Dourif) possessing Damien Karras, aided by 'The Master' (Pazuzu)
notes: Third Exorcist film; direct sequel to the 1973 original
Gemini Killer partly based on the Zodiac Killer
Morgan Creek forced a new exorcism climax with Father Morning
Cameos: Fabio, Patrick Ewing, Larry King, C. Everett Koop; early Samuel L. Jackson role
Colleen Dewhurst is the uncredited voice of Pazuzu

films.title: Night of the Living Dead
altTitles: George A. Romero's Night of the Living Dead
films.basedOn: Night of the Living Dead (1968) by John A. Russo and George A. Romero
films.setting: Rural Pennsylvania farmhouse (opens at a Butler County cemetery)
films.villain: Zombies; human antagonist Harry Cooper (Tom Towles)
notes: Tom Savini's feature directorial debut
Only official remake of the 1968 film
Barbara survives and kills Harry: 'another one for the fire'
Russell Streiner (Johnny in 1968) cameos as Sheriff McClelland

films.title: Child's Play 2
films.basedOn: Characters from Child's Play (1988) by Don Mancini
films.setting: Simpsons' foster home and the Play Pals Good Guy doll factory
films.villain: Chucky, killer Good Guy doll (voice Brad Dourif; in-suit Ed Gale)
notes: Second Child's Play film; set two years after the first; Andy is in foster care
Universal took over the series after MGM/UA shelved it
Chucky dies when Kyle inflates his head with an air hose until it explodes
Poster tagline: 'Sorry Jack... Chucky's back!'
Opened #1 in the US with $10.7M; followed by Child's Play 3 (1991)

films.title: Flatliners
films.setting: Medical school (filmed at Loyola University Chicago)
films.villain: Guilt visions from their pasts, e.g. Billy Mahoney, the boy Nelson bullied and killed
notes: Five medical students stop their hearts to experience death
Oscar nomination for Best Sound Editing
Produced by Michael Douglas; shot by Jan de Bont
Opened #1 at the US box office
2017 follow-up also featured Kiefer Sutherland

films.title: The Witches
films.yearNote: UK release May 25, 1990; US Aug 24, 1990
films.genreNote: dark fantasy family film often listed as horror
films.basedOn: The Witches (novel) by Roald Dahl
films.setting: Hotel Excelsior on the English seaside; opens in Norway
cast: Eva Ernst / The Grand High Witch
films.villain: The Grand High Witch (Anjelica Huston), posing as Eva Ernst
notes: Witches plan to turn the world's children into mice with a potion
Last film Jim Henson worked on; Creature Shop made witch makeup and mice
Roald Dahl disliked the happy ending where Luke becomes human again
Huston won LA Film Critics and National Society of Film Critics Best Actress

films.title: Nightbreed
films.basedOn: Cabal (1988 novella) by Clive Barker
films.setting: Midian, a hidden refuge of monsters under an abandoned cemetery
films.villain: Dr. Philip K. Decker (David Cronenberg), Boone's psychotherapist and a masked serial killer
notes: Director David Cronenberg plays the villain
Baphomet, deity of the Nightbreed, renames Boone 'Cabal'
Score by Danny Elfman
Director's cut restored and released in 2014 via Scream Factory

films.title: Graveyard Shift
films.basedOn: Graveyard Shift (1970 short story) by Stephen King
films.setting: Rat-infested textile mill next to a graveyard (filmed in Harmony, Maine)
films.villain: Giant bat-like rat creature under the mill; sadistic foreman Warwick (Stephen Macht)
notes: Story first ran in Cavalier (Oct 1970); collected in Night Shift (1978)
Mill renamed 'Bachman' as a nod to King's pen name Richard Bachman
Ralph S. Singleton's directorial debut
Opened #1 in the US
King called it 'a quick exploitation picture'

films.title: Gremlins 2: The New Batch
films.basedOn: Characters created by Chris Columbus
films.setting: Clamp Center skyscraper, Manhattan, New York City
films.villain: Gremlins incl. Mohawk (voice Frank Welker) and the Brain Gremlin (voice Tony Randall)
notes: Creature designs by Rick Baker
Catheter's first name honors Christopher Lee's co-star Peter Cushing
Cameos: Hulk Hogan, Leonard Maltin
Looney Tunes segments directed by Chuck Jones
Released June 15, 1990, same day as Dick Tracy

films.title: Leatherface: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre III
films.basedOn: Characters by Kim Henkel and Tobe Hooper
films.villain: Leatherface (R. A. Mihailoff) and the cannibal Sawyer family
notes: Third Texas Chainsaw Massacre film; first by New Line Cinema
Initially rated X; cut 4 min 18 sec to get an R
Leatherface's chainsaw is engraved 'The Saw is Family'
Kane Hodder was stunt coordinator and Mihailoff's stunt double
Refused UK classification in 1990

films.title: Two Evil Eyes
films.yearNote: Italy release Jan 25, 1990; US release Oct 25, 1991 (English Wikipedia calls it a 1991 film)
films.director: George A. Romero and Dario Argento
films.writers: George A. Romero, Dario Argento, Franco Ferrini
films.basedOn: The Facts in the Case of M. Valdemar and The Black Cat by Edgar Allan Poe
films.villain: The 'Others' (Valdemar segment); a vengeful black cat haunting killer Rod Usher (Black Cat)
notes: Romero directed 'Valdemar'; Argento directed 'The Black Cat'
Julie Benz's first acting role
Tom Savini did makeup effects and cameos as the Monomaniac
Romero and Argento first worked together on Dawn of the Dead (1978)

films.title: Tales from the Darkside: The Movie
films.genreNote: comedy horror anthology; spin-off of the TV series
films.writers: Michael McDowell and George A. Romero
films.basedOn: Lot No. 249 (Arthur Conan Doyle); The Cat from Hell (Stephen King); Yuki-onna tale (Lafcadio Hearn)
films.villain: Witch Betty (Deborah Harry) plans to cook Timmy; segments feature a mummy, a killer cat and a gargoyle
notes: Julianne Moore's film debut
Segments: 'Lot 249', 'The Cat from Hell', 'Lover's Vow'
Romero wrote the Stephen King segment 'The Cat from Hell'
Often called 'the true Creepshow 3'
Final line: 'Don't you just love happy endings?'

films.title: Frankenhooker
films.setting: Ho-Ho-Kus, New Jersey and New York City
films.villain: Frankenhooker, Elizabeth rebuilt from prostitutes' body parts; pimp Zorro
notes: Parody of Mary Shelley's Frankenstein
Elizabeth is killed by a remote-controlled lawnmower
Jeffrey's exploding 'super-crack' supplies the body parts
Patty Mullen was a former Penthouse Pet
VHS box played 'Wanna date?' when pressed

films.title: The Guardian
films.writers: William Friedkin, Dan Greenburg, Stephen Volk
films.basedOn: The Nanny by Dan Greenburg
films.villain: Camilla (Jenny Seagrove), a nanny who is an ancient Hamadryad sacrificing babies to a giant tree
notes: Friedkin's first horror film since The Exorcist (1973)
Sam Raimi was first attached but left to make Darkman
TV cut credited to 'Alan Von Smithee'
On Roger Ebert's 'Most Hated Films' list

films.title: Psycho IV: The Beginning
films.yearNote: Showtime premiere Nov 10, 1990
films.basedOn: Characters created by Robert Bloch
films.setting: Bates Motel and Bates house (flashbacks to the 1940s-50s)
films.villain: Norman Bates and his 'Mother' personality
notes: Fourth and final original Psycho film; prequel and sequel
Anthony Perkins's last time as Norman Bates
Writer Joseph Stefano also wrote the 1960 Psycho
Norman calls radio host Fran Ambrose as 'Ed'
Aired in a Psycho retrospective hosted by Janet Leigh; filmed at Universal Studios Florida

films.title: Troll 2
films.genreNote: Italian-made dark fantasy horror; cult 'worst movie'
films.setting: Nilbog, a rural farming town (filmed in Morgan and Porterville, Utah)
films.villain: Vegetarian goblins of Nilbog led by druid witch Creedence Leonore Gielgud
notes: Features goblins, not trolls; unrelated to Troll (1986)
Nilbog is 'goblin' spelled backwards
Famous scene: Arnold screams 'Oh my God!'
Joshua defeats the goblins with a double-decker bologna sandwich
Star Michael Stephenson directed the 2009 documentary Best Worst Movie

films.title: Bride of Re-Animator
films.yearNote: Premiered at TIFF Sep 8, 1990; US release Feb 22, 1991
films.writers: Woody Keith and Rick Fry (adapted with Brian Yuzna)
films.basedOn: Herbert West-Reanimator by H. P. Lovecraft
films.villain: Dr. Carl Hill's reanimated head with bat wings (David Gale) and his zombies
notes: Second Re-Animator film
Title is an homage to Bride of Frankenstein
West builds a woman around the heart of Dan's dead fiancee Meg Halsey
Barbara Crampton did not return

films.title: Hardware
films.basedOn: SHOK! (2000 AD comic story) by Steve MacManus and Kevin O'Neill, credited after a lawsuit
films.villain: M.A.R.K. 13, a self-repairing military combat robot
notes: Richard Stanley's feature directorial debut
Robot named for Mark 13: 'No flesh shall be spared'
Fleetway successfully sued for plagiarism of 2000 AD's 'SHOK!'
Lemmy cameos as a water taxi driver
Robot's weakness is humidity; Jill kills it with a shower

films.title: The Silence of the Lambs
films.basedOn: The Silence of the Lambs (1988 novel) by Thomas Harris
films.setting: FBI Academy, Quantico, Virginia; Baltimore asylum; Memphis; Ohio
films.villain: Buffalo Bill (Jame Gumb, Ted Levine), serial killer who skins women; Hannibal Lecter (Anthony Hopkins), imprisoned cannibal psychiatrist
notes: Won Oscar Big Five (Picture, Director, Actor, Actress, Adapted Screenplay); only horror film to win Best Picture
AFI ranks Hannibal Lecter the No. 1 film villain and Clarice Starling the No. 6 hero
AFI No. 21 quote: 'I ate his liver with some fava beans and a nice Chianti'
Second Lecter film after Manhunter (1986); sequel Hannibal (2001), prequel Red Dragon (2002)
Death's-head moth clue; Bill's dog is Precious; Goodbye Horses by Q Lazzarus plays in mirror scene

films.title: Freddy's Dead: The Final Nightmare
films.writers: Michael De Luca (story by Rachel Talalay)
films.basedOn: Characters by Wes Craven
cast: Teen on TV (credited as Oprah Noodlemantra)
films.villain: Freddy Krueger (Robert Englund); his daughter Maggie kills him with a pipe bomb
notes: Sixth A Nightmare on Elm Street film; followed by Wes Craven's New Nightmare (1994)
Last ~10 minutes in 3D; New Line Cinema's first 3D release
Rachel Talalay's feature directorial debut
Cameos: Johnny Depp, Roseanne Barr, Tom Arnold, Alice Cooper; Iggy Pop sings end-credits song
$12.9M opening was the series' best until Freddy vs. Jason

films.title: The People Under the Stairs
films.villain: The Robesons, 'Mommy and Daddy' (Wendy Robie, Everett McGill), incestuous sibling landlords
notes: McGill and Robie had played married couple Big Ed and Nadine Hurley on TV's Twin Peaks
Inspired by a 1978 LA news story: burglars' break-in exposed children locked up by parents
Stolen children are kept in the basement; Daddy's Rottweiler is named Prince
Opened at No. 1 with about $5.5M
Jordan Peele's Monkeypaw announced a remake in 2020

films.title: Child's Play 3
films.basedOn: Characters by Don Mancini
films.villain: Chucky (voice Brad Dourif), revived when his blood drips into molten plastic at the Play Pals factory
notes: Third Child's Play film; released 9 months after Child's Play 2 but set 8 years later
Andy is 16, played by Justin Whalin (Alex Vincent did not return)
Climax in a carnival horror ride; Chucky is shredded by a giant fan
Filmed at Kemper Military School, Boonville, Missouri
UK press linked it to the James Bulger murder; police found no link. Next: Bride of Chucky (1998)

films.title: Critters 3
films.yearNote: direct-to-video, Dec 11, 1991
films.writers: David J. Schow (story by Rupert Harvey, Barry Opper)
films.setting: a run-down apartment tenement (not Grover's Bend)
films.villain: The Critters (Krites); voices by the Chiodo brothers
notes: Leonardo DiCaprio's film debut
Third Critters film; first not set in Grover's Bend
Shot simultaneously with Critters 4 (Feb-Jul 1991); ends on a cliffhanger

films.title: Cape Fear
films.genreNote: southern gothic psychological thriller, often listed as horror
films.basedOn: The Executioners (1957 novel) by John D. MacDonald; remake of Cape Fear (1962)
films.setting: New Essex, North Carolina (fictional); Cape Fear River
films.villain: Max Cady (Robert De Niro), released rapist stalking his former public defender
notes: Oscar nominations: De Niro (Best Actor) and Juliette Lewis (Best Supporting Actress)
1962 stars Robert Mitchum, Gregory Peck (final theatrical role) and Martin Balsam appear
Spielberg traded it to Scorsese for Schindler's List; Amblin produced, Spielberg uncredited
First Scorsese film to gross over $100M; 7th Scorsese-De Niro collaboration
Parodied in The Simpsons episode Cape Feare (1993)

films.title: Body Parts
films.writers: Eric Red, Norman Snider (story by Patricia Herskovic, Joyce Taylor)
films.basedOn: Novel Choice Cuts by Pierre Boileau and Thomas Narcejac
films.villain: Executed serial killer Charley Fletcher (John Walsh), whose transplanted limbs influence recipients
notes: Psychologist gets a killer's arm; the legs and other arm go to two other men
Paramount pulled Milwaukee ads after Jeffrey Dahmer's crimes were discovered
Loek Dikker's score features a singing saw

films.title: Popcorn
films.director: Mark Herrier (replaced Alan Ormsby during filming)
films.writers: Alan Ormsby per Wikipedia lead; credited screenplay Tod Hackett, story Mitchell Smith
films.setting: Dreamland, an abandoned movie theater hosting a horror marathon
films.villain: Toby D'Amato (Tom Villard), burned at a Possessor screening; wears masks of his victims
notes: Marathon films: Mosquito (3D), The Attack of the Amazing Electrified Man (Shock-o-Scope), The Stench (Odorama)
Filmed entirely in Kingston, Jamaica; Bob Clark was an uncredited producer
Jill Schoelen replaced original lead Amy O'Neill

films.title: Candyman
films.basedOn: Short story The Forbidden by Clive Barker (set in Liverpool)
films.villain: Candyman (Tony Todd), hook-handed ghost of a slave's son lynched in the late 1800s
notes: Summoned by saying his name five times in a mirror; hook for a right hand; bees
Score by Philip Glass
Over 200,000 real bees used; Tony Todd got $1,000 per sting (23 stings)
Sequels: Farewell to the Flesh (1995), Day of the Dead (1999), Candyman (2021)
Premiered at TIFF Midnight Madness, Sept 1992; Madsen was hypnotized for some scenes

films.title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
films.basedOn: Dracula (1897 novel) by Bram Stoker
films.villain: Count Dracula / Vlad the Impaler (Gary Oldman); brides include Monica Bellucci
notes: Won 3 of 4 Oscar noms: Costume Design (Eiko Ishioka), Makeup, Sound Editing
First vampire film and only Dracula adaptation to win Oscars
Line: 'I've crossed oceans of time to find you'
Winona Ryder brought the script to Coppola; effects done in-camera by Roman Coppola, no CGI
November-record $30.5M opening; end song Love Song for a Vampire by Annie Lennox

films.title: Army of Darkness
altTitles: Bruce Campbell vs. Army of Darkness
Evil Dead III: Army of Darkness
films.yearNote: Premiered Sitges Oct 9, 1992; US release Feb 19, 1993
films.setting: Medieval England, circa 1300; ends at S-Mart
films.villain: Evil Ash (Bruce Campbell) leading the Deadite Army of Darkness
notes: Third Evil Dead film, sequel to Evil Dead II (1987)
Ash botches the words 'Klaatu barada nikto' needed to take the Necronomicon
Catchphrase 'Hail to the king, baby'; Ash drives a 1973 Oldsmobile Delta 88
Original ending: Ash oversleeps into post-apocalyptic London; Universal wanted the S-Mart ending
Won the 1994 Saturn Award for Best Horror Film

films.title: Braindead
films.yearNote: NZ Aug 1992; US release Feb 1993 as Dead Alive
films.genreNote: New Zealand zombie comedy splatter film
films.writers: Stephen Sinclair, Fran Walsh, Peter Jackson
films.villain: Vera Cosgrove (Elizabeth Moody), zombified by a Sumatran rat-monkey bite
notes: Sumatran rat-monkey is smuggled from Skull Island to Wellington Zoo
Lawn mower zombie massacre reputedly used 300 litres of fake blood
Retitled Dead Alive in the US because of a rival film titled Brain Dead
Peter Jackson cameos as the undertaker's assistant; shot on Super 16mm
Simon Pegg cites it as an influence on Shaun of the Dead

films.title: Hellraiser III: Hell on Earth
films.writers: Peter Atkins (story by Peter Atkins, Tony Randel)
films.basedOn: Characters by Clive Barker
films.setting: New York City (filmed in Greensboro, North Carolina)
films.villain: Pinhead (Doug Bradley), freed from the Pillar of Souls; new Cenobites incl. Pistonhead, Camerahead, Barbie, CD
notes: Third Hellraiser film; first shot in the US and first Dimension Films release via Miramax
Pinhead is split from his human self, WWI British Captain Elliott Spencer
Monroe's nightclub is The Boiler Room; Armored Saint cameo; Motorhead song Hellraiser
Followed by Hellraiser: Bloodline (1996)

films.title: Alien 3
films.writers: David Giler, Walter Hill, Larry Ferguson (story by Vincent Ward)
films.basedOn: Characters by Dan O'Bannon and Ronald Shusett
films.villain: Xenomorph 'Dragon' born from a dog (Tom Woodruff Jr. in suit); Weyland-Yutani wants Ripley's Queen embryo
notes: Third Alien film; David Fincher's feature directorial debut, which he later disowned
Ripley sacrifices herself in a furnace as the Queen bursts from her chest
Oscar-nominated for Visual Effects, lost to Death Becomes Her
Rejected drafts include William Gibson's script and Vincent Ward's wooden planet of monks
2003 Assembly Cut has the Alien born from an ox; followed by Alien Resurrection (1997)

films.title: Sleepwalkers
films.setting: Travis, Indiana (prologue in Bodega Bay, California)
films.villain: Charles and Mary Brady (Brian Krause, Alice Krige), incestuous mother-son shapeshifting werecat energy vampires
notes: First Stephen King screenplay written for film rather than adapted from his own work
Sleepwalkers feed on virgins' life force; domestic cats are their only weakness
Deputy's cat Clovis (played by Sparks) leads the cats that kill Mary
Cameos: Clive Barker, Tobe Hooper, John Landis, Joe Dante; Mark Hamill uncredited

films.title: Pet Sematary Two
films.basedOn: Sequel to Pet Sematary (1989), from Stephen King's 1983 novel
films.villain: Sheriff Gus Gilbert (Clancy Brown) and the dog Zowie, revived at the Mi'kmaq burial ground; undead Renee
notes: Stephen King had his name removed before release
Mary Lambert directed both Pet Sematary films
Edward Furlong was cast after Terminator 2; filmed in Coweta County, Georgia
Undead Renee's last cry: 'Dead is better!'

films.title: Innocent Blood
films.villain: Mob boss Sal 'the Shark' Macelli (Robert Loggia), turned vampire, building a vampire crime family
notes: Future Sopranos actors Tony Sirico, Tony Lip and David Proval play gangsters
Cameos: Sam Raimi, Dario Argento, Frank Oz, Tom Savini; Don Rickles plays lawyer Manny Bergman
Box-office bomb: about $4.9M on a $20M budget

films.title: Buffy the Vampire Slayer
films.villain: Lothos (Rutger Hauer), elder vampire; acolyte Amilyn (Paul Reubens)
notes: Hilary Swank's debut role (Kimberly); uncredited Ben Affleck, Ricki Lake, Seth Green
Merrick is Buffy's Watcher; she is the Slayer, the 'Chosen One'
Whedon, unhappy with the film, made the TV series on The WB five years later
Shot in five weeks around Luke Perry's 90210 schedule; sold to Dolly Parton's Sandollar

films.title: Dr. Giggles
cast: Dr. Evan Rendell Jr. / Dr. Giggles
films.villain: Dr. Evan Rendell Jr., 'Dr. Giggles' (Larry Drake), asylum escapee who kills with medical tools
notes: Giggles wants heroine Jennifer's heart; she has a heart condition
Final line to camera: 'Is there a doctor in the house?'
First film from Largo Entertainment's first-look deal with Dark Horse Comics

films.title: Man Bites Dog
altTitles: C'est arrive pres de chez vous
films.yearNote: Premiered Cannes May 1992; US release Jan 1993
films.genreNote: Belgian black comedy crime mockumentary, often listed as horror
films.director: Remy Belvaux, Andre Bonzel, Benoit Poelvoorde
films.writers: Remy Belvaux, Andre Bonzel, Benoit Poelvoorde, Vincent Tavier
films.villain: Ben (Benoit Poelvoorde), serial killer filmed by a documentary crew that becomes complicit
notes: Shot in black and white on 16mm for about BEF 1 million (~$33,000)
Won the International Critics' Prize at Cannes 1992; rated NC-17 in the US
French title means 'It Happened Near Your Home', from a Le Soir column
Poelvoorde's real parents and grandparents played his family

films.title: Children of the Corn II: The Final Sacrifice
altTitles: Children of the Corn II: Deadly Harvest
films.yearNote: Released Italy/France 1992; US theatrical release Jan 29, 1993
films.basedOn: Sequel to Children of the Corn (1984), from Stephen King's Children of the Corn
films.villain: Micah (Ryan Bollman), possessed by He Who Walks Behind the Rows
notes: Set two days after the first film; Gatlin's surviving children are taken in by Hemingford
Last Children of the Corn film released theatrically until 2023
Made back-to-back with Hellraiser III; both among the earliest Dimension Films releases

films.title: Critters 4
films.yearNote: direct-to-video; Wikipedia infobox date Oct 14, 1992 (a 1998 VHS release is also listed)
films.writers: David J. Schow, Joseph Lyle (story by Rupert Harvey, Barry Opper)
films.setting: a space station in the year 2045
films.villain: The Krites (Critters); TerraCor's Counselor Tetra (Terrence Mann)
notes: Fourth Critters film, shot simultaneously with Critters 3 in 1991
Charlie is frozen in a pod for over 50 years; darker, less comedic tone
Station computer 'Angela' obeys only the opposite of orders

films.title: Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me
altTitles: Twin Peaks: The Last Seven Days of Laura Palmer (Japan)
films.genreNote: psychological horror; prequel to the Twin Peaks TV series
films.basedOn: Twin Peaks TV series by Mark Frost and David Lynch
films.setting: Twin Peaks and Deer Meadow, Washington
films.villain: BOB (Frank Silva), spirit possessing Laura's father Leland Palmer (Ray Wise)
notes: Prequel: Laura Palmer's last seven days; opens with the Teresa Banks murder
Moira Kelly replaced Lara Flynn Boyle as Donna; Kiefer Sutherland plays Agent Sam Stanley
Competed for the Palme d'Or at Cannes 1992; US box-office bomb
Won the Saturn Award for Best Music (Angelo Badalamenti)
BFI (2019) ranked it the fourth-best film of the 1990s

films.title: The Lawnmower Man
films.basedOn: Nominally Stephen King's 1975 short story The Lawnmower Man (King had his name removed)
films.villain: Jobe Smith (Jeff Fahey), gardener turned telekinetic digital being by VR experiments
notes: King sued and won removal of his name, plus a $2.5M settlement
Only link to King's story: a lawnmower killing of Harold Parkette
Rewritten from an unrelated VR script titled Cyber God
Ending: every phone on Earth rings, signaling Jobe's digital birth
Sequel: Lawnmower Man 2: Beyond Cyberspace (1996)

films.title: Ghostwatch
films.genreNote: BBC TV film; pseudo-documentary presented as live
films.villain: Poltergeist 'Pipes' (Keith Ferrari; voiced by director Lesley Manning)
notes: Aired on BBC1 Halloween night 1992 as if live; the BBC got about 30,000 calls
Never repeated on UK television
Inspired by the Enfield Poltergeist; compared to Welles' War of the Worlds broadcast

films.title: Jason Goes to Hell: The Final Friday
films.writers: Dean Lorey, Jay Huguely (screenplay); story by Jay Huguely, Adam Marcus
films.basedOn: Characters by Victor Miller (Friday the 13th)
films.villain: Jason Voorhees (Kane Hodder) - after an FBI sting kills him, his heart/spirit possesses others; only a blood relative with a magic dagger can kill him
notes: 9th Friday the 13th film; first released by New Line Cinema (Paramount released the first eight)
Final shot: Freddy Krueger's clawed glove drags Jason's mask underground, teasing Freddy vs. Jason
Features the Necronomicon and Kandarian dagger from Evil Dead II
Jason's living relatives: half-sister Diana Kimble, her daughter Jessica, and baby Stephanie
Adam Marcus's directorial debut; bounty hunter Creighton Duke hunts Jason

films.title: Leprechaun
films.villain: The Leprechaun (Warwick Davis), hunting for his stolen pot of gold
notes: Jennifer Aniston's first major film role (she had an uncredited bit in Mac and Me, 1988)
Killed with a four-leaf clover; he wants all 100 gold coins and compulsively shines shoes
Writer-director Mark Jones was inspired by Lucky Charms commercials
First Trimark in-house production released theatrically; launched the Leprechaun franchise

films.title: Body Snatchers
films.yearNote: Premiered in competition at Cannes May 1993; US limited release Jan 14, 1994
films.writers: Stuart Gordon, Dennis Paoli, Nicholas St. John (screenplay); story by Raymond Cistheri, Larry Cohen
films.basedOn: The Body Snatchers (1955 novel) by Jack Finney
films.villain: Pod people - emotionless duplicates grown from giant plantlike pods
notes: Third film adaptation of Finney's novel, after Invasion of the Body Snatchers (1956 and 1978)
Producer Robert H. Solo also produced the 1978 version
Famous warning: "They get you when you sleep"
Roger Ebert gave it four stars

films.title: Cronos
films.yearNote: Festival premiere Nov 27, 1992; Mexico theatrical release Dec 3, 1993
films.villain: Dying businessman Dieter de la Guardia (Claudio Brook) and his nephew Angel (Ron Perlman), who hunt the Cronos device
notes: Guillermo del Toro's first feature film
Cronos device: scarab-shaped clockwork made by an alchemist in 1536; grants eternal life and bloodlust
Antique dealer Jesus Gris finds the device hidden in an archangel statue
Mexico's Best Foreign Language Film submission (66th Oscars); not nominated
First of several del Toro films with Federico Luppi and Ron Perlman

films.title: The Dark Half
films.basedOn: The Dark Half (1989 novel) by Stephen King
films.setting: Maine (Sheriff Alan Pangborn of Castle Rock)
films.villain: George Stark - writer Thad Beaumont's pen-name alter ego come to life (also played by Timothy Hutton)
notes: Stark is linked to Thad's absorbed fraternal twin; a flock of sparrows (agents of Death) carries Stark away
Stark's bloody calling card says the sparrows are flying again
Royal Dano's final film role
Shot 1990-91 but shelved two years due to Orion Pictures' financial trouble

films.title: Needful Things
films.basedOn: Needful Things (1991 novel) by Stephen King
films.villain: Leland Gaunt (Max von Sydow), devilish owner of the shop Needful Things
notes: Gaunt trades coveted items for pranks on neighbors, setting Castle Rock against itself
Amanda Plummer won the Saturn Award for Best Supporting Actress
TBS aired a 4-hour version in 1996 with over an hour of extra footage
Gaunt survives the blast and leaves, saying he'll meet Pangborn's grandson in 2053

films.title: Return of the Living Dead 3
altTitles: Return of the Living Dead III
films.setting: A U.S. military base and city sewers
films.villain: Zombies reanimated by 2-4-5 Trioxin gas, including Julie, who pierces herself to suppress her hunger for brains
notes: Third Return of the Living Dead film; Curt revives his dead girlfriend Julie with Trioxin
Brian Peck is the only actor to appear in all three ROTLD films
Director Anthony Hickox cameos as a scientist killed by a test zombie

films.title: Ticks
films.yearNote: US direct-to-video release May 24, 1994
films.setting: Woodland youth camp (teens from Los Angeles); shot at Big Bear Lake, California
films.villain: Giant mutated ticks, created when a marijuana grower's illegal plant steroid leaks onto a tick nest
notes: Clint Howard plays grower Jarvis Tanner; Rance Howard plays Sheriff Parker
Mutated tick saliva causes hallucinations
Produced by Brian Yuzna

films.title: Pumpkinhead II: Blood Wings
films.yearNote: MIFED (Italy) Oct 1993; US direct-to-video Oct 19, 1994
films.villain: Pumpkinhead (Mark McCracken) - resurrected Tommy, deformed offspring of Pumpkinhead murdered in 1958
notes: Sequel to Pumpkinhead (1988); Lance Henriksen declined to return
Cast includes Soleil Moon Frye, Linnea Quigley, Kane Hodder and Roger Clinton Jr.
Tie-in PC game: Bloodwings: Pumpkinhead's Revenge (1995)

films.title: Body Bags
films.setting: Morgue wraparound; The Gas Station is near Haddonfield, Illinois
films.villain: Anthology: escaped serial killer (The Gas Station), alien hair-transplant parasite (Hair), executed killer's transplanted eye (Eye)
notes: Segments: The Gas Station and Hair (Carpenter), Eye (Hooper)
Cameos include Wes Craven, Sam Raimi, Roger Corman, Tom Arnold and Tobe Hooper
Showtime planned it as a Tales from the Crypt-style series before making it a film
Premiered Aug 8, 1993

films.title: Leprechaun 2
altTitles: One Wedding and Lots of Funerals
films.basedOn: Characters by Mark Jones
films.villain: Lubdan the Leprechaun (Warwick Davis), seeking a bride from the O'Day bloodline
notes: Leprechaun turns 1,000 on St. Patrick's Day; bride is claimed if she sneezes 3 times with no blessing
His weakness here is cast iron
UK title: One Wedding and Lots of Funerals
Last theatrically released Leprechaun film until Leprechaun: Origins (2014)

films.title: Wes Craven's New Nightmare
films.basedOn: Characters by Wes Craven
films.villain: An ancient entity in the guise of Freddy Krueger (Robert Englund) breaking into the real world
notes: 7th Nightmare on Elm Street film; meta-story with cast and crew playing themselves
Working title: A Nightmare on Elm Street 7: The Ascension
Used real footage of 1994 Northridge earthquake damage
Lowest-grossing film in the series; opened against Pulp Fiction
Made for the original's 10th anniversary; seen as a precursor to Scream (1996)

films.title: Interview with the Vampire
films.basedOn: Interview with the Vampire (1976 novel) by Anne Rice
films.setting: New Orleans (from 1791) and Paris (1870); framed by a 1991 San Francisco interview
films.villain: Lestat de Lioncourt (Tom Cruise); also Santiago and the Paris coven of the Theatre des Vampires
notes: River Phoenix was cast as Molloy but died; Christian Slater replaced him and donated his salary
Cruise and Pitt won the Razzie for Worst Screen Couple (tied with The Specialist)
End credits: Guns N' Roses cover of Sympathy for the Devil
Tom Cruise got a record $10M; Anne Rice first opposed his casting, then praised him
Sequel: Queen of the Damned (2002)

films.title: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein
films.basedOn: Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus (1818) by Mary Shelley
films.setting: Geneva and Ingolstadt; Arctic frame story (1794)
films.villain: The Creature (Robert De Niro), built from Waldman's killer's body and Waldman's brain
notes: Produced by Francis Ford Coppola after Bram Stoker's Dracula (1992)
Victor revives Elizabeth on Justine's body; she sets herself on fire
Opened #2 in the US behind Stargate; #1 in the UK for two weeks
Co-writer Frank Darabont publicly disliked the finished film

films.title: Wolf
films.writers: Jim Harrison, Wesley Strick (uncredited Elaine May)
films.villain: Stewart Swinton (James Spader), Will's scheming protege who turns werewolf after Will bites him
notes: Book editor Will Randall is bitten by a wolf on a Vermont road
Score by Ennio Morricone; Rick Baker earned a Saturn makeup nomination
Won the Saturn Award for Best Writing
David Schwimmer has a bit part as a cop
Release delayed 6-8 months to reshoot the ending

films.title: The Crow
films.genreNote: gothic supernatural superhero film often listed as horror
films.basedOn: The Crow (1989 comic) by James O'Barr
films.villain: Crime boss Top Dollar (Michael Wincott) and gang members T-Bird, Tin-Tin, Funboy and Skank
notes: Brandon Lee was fatally shot by a prop gun (squib load) on set Mar 31, 1993, Wilmington, NC
Lee's final film; finished with double Chad Stahelski and digital face replacement
Paramount dropped it after Lee's death; Miramax released it; dedicated to Lee and fiancee Eliza Hutton
Opened #1, Miramax's biggest opening ever at the time
Chart-topping soundtrack; The Cure's Burn is the main theme

films.title: In the Mouth of Madness
films.yearNote: Premiered Fantasy Filmfest (Germany) Aug 10, 1994; US release Feb 3, 1995
films.villain: Horror novelist Sutter Cane (Jurgen Prochnow), whose books unleash the Old Ones
notes: Third of Carpenter's Apocalypse Trilogy, after The Thing and Prince of Darkness
Title plays on H.P. Lovecraft's At the Mountains of Madness
Hayden Christensen's film debut, as a paper boy
Insurance investigator Trent hunts missing author Cane for publisher Arcane
Theme inspired by Metallica's Enter Sandman (Carpenter couldn't get the rights)

films.title: Cemetery Man
films.yearNote: US release Apr 26, 1996 (October Films)
films.basedOn: Dellamorte Dellamore (novel) by Tiziano Sclavi
films.setting: Buffalora, a small Italian town's cemetery
films.villain: Returners - the dead who rise as zombies within seven nights of burial
notes: Sclavi's comic hero Dylan Dog was visually based on Rupert Everett
Assistant Gnaghi can say only one word: Gna
Cemetery gate inscription: RESURRECTURIS
Martin Scorsese called it one of the best Italian films of the 1990s

films.title: Brainscan
films.writers: Andrew Kevin Walker (screenplay); story by Brian Owens
films.villain: The Trickster (T. Ryder Smith), host of the Brainscan CD-ROM game
notes: Lonely teen plays interactive game Brainscan, then real murders match his game kills
Soundtrack includes White Zombie, Primus, Mudhoney and Butthole Surfers

films.title: Nightwatch
films.villain: Police superintendent Peter Wormer (Ulf Pilgaard), a serial killer and necrophiliac former night watchman
notes: Law student Martin takes a night-watchman job at a morgue
Remade in English by Bornedal in 1997, with a script by Steven Soderbergh
Sequel: Nightwatch: Demons Are Forever (2023)
Won the Robert Award for Best Danish Film

films.title: The Stand
films.genreNote: ABC TV miniseries (4 parts, aired May 8-12, 1994)
films.basedOn: The Stand (1978 novel) by Stephen King
films.setting: Post-pandemic U.S.: Boulder, Colorado vs. Las Vegas
films.villain: Randall Flagg, the Dark Man (Jamey Sheridan)
notes: Engineered flu Project Blue, nicknamed Captain Trips, kills 99.4% of humanity
Good survivors form the Boulder Free Zone; Flagg rules Las Vegas
Stephen King cameos as Teddy Weizak; Kareem Abdul-Jabbar plays The Monster Shouter
Uncredited: Kathy Bates (Rae Flowers) and Ed Harris (Gen. Starkey)
6 Emmy nominations; won for makeup and sound mixing

films.title: Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Next Generation
altTitles: The Return of the Texas Chainsaw Massacre
films.yearNote: Shot 1993; premiered SXSW Mar 12, 1995; re-cut Next Generation version released Aug 29, 1997
films.setting: Rural Texas, prom night (dated May 22, 1994; 1996 in re-cut)
films.villain: Leatherface (Robert Jacks) and Vilmer Slaughter (Matthew McConaughey), who has a remote-controlled mechanical leg
notes: 4th Texas Chainsaw film; Kim Henkel co-wrote the 1974 original and made his directing debut here
Zellweger and McConaughey were unknowns; release was delayed until after their breakouts
Cameos by original-film stars Marilyn Burns, Paul A. Partain and John Dugan
Working title: The Taxidermist: Texas Chainsaw Massacre 4

films.title: Hocus Pocus
films.genreNote: Disney fantasy comedy; Halloween favorite often in horror-adjacent trivia
films.writers: Mick Garris, Neil Cuthbert (screenplay); story by David Kirschner, Mick Garris
films.villain: The Sanderson sisters - witches Winifred, Mary and Sarah
notes: Witches return when a virgin lights the Black Flame Candle on Halloween
Prologue Oct 31, 1693: Binx is cursed to live as an immortal black cat
Bette Midler performs I Put a Spell on You
Initially a box-office flop (~$16.5M loss) that became a cult classic via TV airings
Garry and Penny Marshall cameo; sequel Hocus Pocus 2 (2022, Disney+)

films.title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
altTitles: Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas
films.genreNote: stop-motion animated musical fantasy; Halloween-themed, horror-adjacent
films.writers: Caroline Thompson (screenplay); adaptation by Michael McDowell
films.basedOn: Poem by Tim Burton
films.villain: Oogie Boogie (Ken Page), a gambling bogeyman
notes: Directed by Henry Selick, not Tim Burton; grew from a 1982 Burton poem
First animated film nominated for the Best Visual Effects Oscar
Jack Skellington is the Pumpkin King; Halloween Town calls Santa Sandy Claws
Danny Elfman wrote the score and songs
Added to the National Film Registry in 2023; reissued in Disney Digital 3-D in 2006

films.title: The Tommyknockers
films.genreNote: ABC TV miniseries (2 parts, aired May 9-10, 1993)
films.basedOn: The Tommyknockers (1987 novel) by Stephen King
films.villain: A buried alien spaceship whose influence transforms Haven's townspeople
notes: Writer Bobbi Anderson digs up the alien craft in the woods
Filmed in New Zealand, standing in for New England
Original director Lewis Teague was fired on day two of filming

films.title: Seven
films.genreNote: crime thriller often listed as horror
films.setting: Unnamed crime-ridden city (filmed in Los Angeles)
films.villain: John Doe - serial killer staging murders on the seven deadly sins; played by Kevin Spacey
notes: Victims: gluttony, greed, sloth, lust, pride, then envy and wrath; Tracy's severed head is delivered in a box
Famous line: "What's in the box?" (Mills/Brad Pitt)
Spacey asked to be left out of marketing and the opening credits to hide the killer's identity
Only Oscar nomination: Best Film Editing (Richard Francis-Bruce); MTV Best Movie and Best Villain (Spacey)
Seventh-highest-grossing film of 1995; $14M opening was then the record for September

films.title: Species
films.villain: Sil - extraterrestrial-human hybrid seeking to mate; Natasha Henstridge (adult), Michelle Williams (young)
notes: Natasha Henstridge's film debut
Sil's alien form was designed by H. R. Giger (Alien)
Scenes filmed in Utah and at the Arecibo Observatory, Puerto Rico
First of the Species franchise: Species II (theatrical), then TV sequels Species III and Species - The Awakening

films.title: Halloween: The Curse of Michael Myers
films.basedOn: Characters by John Carpenter and Debra Hill
cast: Paul Rudd (credited as Paul Stephen Rudd)
films.villain: Michael Myers (George P. Wilbur), controlled by the Cult of Thorn; the Man in Black is revealed as Dr. Terence Wynn
notes: Sixth Halloween film; Donald Pleasence's final Loomis role - he died Feb 2, 1995, film dedicated to him
Paul Rudd's feature film debut, as the adult Tommy Doyle from Halloween (1978)
Introduces Thorn, an ancient Druid curse driving Michael to kill his family on Halloween
Producer's Cut workprint (45 min of alternate footage) officially released by Scream Factory in 2014
Followed by Halloween H20 (1998), which ignores the Jamie Lloyd films

films.title: Candyman: Farewell to the Flesh
films.writers: Rand Ravich and Mark Kruger (story by Clive Barker)
films.basedOn: Sequel to Candyman (1992), adapted from Clive Barker's story "The Forbidden"
films.villain: Candyman - spirit of Daniel Robitaille, murdered son of a slave; Tony Todd
notes: Second Candyman film; moves the story from Chicago to New Orleans
Candyman's real name revealed as Daniel Robitaille
Score by Philip Glass
Followed by Candyman 3: Day of the Dead (1999)

films.title: Tales from the Crypt Presents: Demon Knight
altTitles: Tales from the Crypt: Demon Knight
films.writers: Mark Bishop, Ethan Reiff and Cyrus Voris
films.basedOn: Tales from the Crypt (EC Comics / HBO series)
films.setting: Isolated New Mexico town; boarding house in a decommissioned church
films.villain: The Collector - demon in human form; Billy Zane
notes: The Collector hunts the last of seven keys, an artifact holding the blood of Jesus Christ
Crypt Keeper (voice John Kassir) appears in the intro and outro
First Tales from the Crypt feature; followed by Bordello of Blood (1996)
John Larroquette has an uncredited cameo as Slasher

films.title: Lord of Illusions
films.basedOn: "The Last Illusion" by Clive Barker (Books of Blood Vol. 6, 1985)
films.setting: Los Angeles; prologue in the Mojave Desert, 1982
films.villain: Nix, "The Puritan" - cult-leading sorcerer; Daniel von Bargen
notes: First screen appearance of Barker's occult detective Harry D'Amour
Barker's third film as writer-director, after Hellraiser and Nightbreed
Nix is a new villain created for the film, not in the original story
MGM cut about 12.5 minutes; an unrated director's cut was released later

films.title: The Prophecy
films.villain: Archangel Gabriel (Christopher Walken), waging a second war in Heaven
notes: Gregory Widen's feature directorial debut; first of The Prophecy series (four sequels)
Gabriel seeks the dark soul of Korean War veteran Col. Arnold Hawthorne
Viggo Mortensen plays Lucifer
Development titles: Daemons and God's Army

films.title: Village of the Damned
films.basedOn: The Midwich Cuckoos (1957) by John Wyndham; remake of the 1960 film
films.setting: Midwich, fictional coastal town in Marin County, California
films.villain: Ten psychic children born after a town blackout, led by Mara Chaffee (Lindsey Haun)
notes: Christopher Reeve's last theatrical film before his May 1995 riding accident paralysis
Moves the story from England to Northern California
Tagline: "Beware the Children"
Razzie nominee for Worst Remake/Sequel (lost to The Scarlet Letter)

films.title: Vampire in Brooklyn
films.writers: Charles Q. Murphy, Michael Lucker, Chris Parker (story by Eddie Murphy, Vernon Lynch, Charles Q. Murphy)
films.villain: Maximillian - Caribbean vampire, seemingly the last of his kind; Eddie Murphy
notes: Final film of Eddie Murphy's exclusive Paramount contract, begun with 48 Hrs. (1982)
Murphy plays three roles: Maximillian, Preacher Pauly and mobster Guido
Max must turn Rita, the only known half-vampire, before the next full moon
Stuntwoman Sonja Davis, Bassett's double, died after a 42-foot fall during filming

films.title: The Mangler
films.writers: Tobe Hooper, Stephen David Brooks, Peter Welbeck (Harry Alan Towers)
films.basedOn: "The Mangler" by Stephen King (1972 short story, in Night Shift, 1978)
films.setting: Gartley's Blue Ribbon Laundry in an unnamed town
films.villain: The Mangler - a demon-possessed industrial laundry press; owner Bill Gartley (Robert Englund) feeds it virgin sacrifices
notes: Town elders sacrifice virgin daughters to the machine on their 16th birthdays
Spawned DTV sequels The Mangler 2 and The Mangler Reborn

films.title: Leprechaun 3
films.yearNote: Direct-to-video, June 27, 1995
films.basedOn: Characters by Mark Jones
films.villain: The Leprechaun (Lubdan) - Warwick Davis
notes: Third Leprechaun film; followed by Leprechaun 4: In Space (1997)
Highest-selling independent direct-to-video film of 1995
Each of the leprechaun's gold coins grants its holder one wish
Shot in 14 days, with only one day in Las Vegas

films.title: Castle Freak
films.yearNote: Direct-to-video, Nov 1995
films.villain: Giorgio Orsino, the Freak - the Duchess's tortured son kept in the dungeon; Jonathan Fuller
notes: Reunites Re-Animator's Stuart Gordon, Jeffrey Combs and Barbara Crampton
Shot in a castle in Italy owned by producer Charles Band
Gordon and Paoli drew on H. P. Lovecraft's story "The Outsider"
Remade in 2020

films.title: The Day of the Beast
films.genreNote: Spanish black comedy with satanic horror themes
films.writers: Jorge Guerricaechevarria and Alex de la Iglesia
films.villain: The Antichrist, whose birth the priest tries to prevent
notes: A Basque priest teams with a metalhead and a TV occultist to stop the Antichrist's birth
Marketed as "a satanic comedy"
Won 6 Goya Awards incl. Best Director and Best New Actor (Santiago Segura)
Finale at Madrid's Gate of Europe towers

films.title: Scream
films.villain: Ghostface - revealed as Billy Loomis (Skeet Ulrich) and Stu Macher (Matthew Lillard); voice Roger L. Jackson
notes: Developed as Scary Movie; inspired by the Gainesville Ripper murders
Barrymore was first cast as Sidney but took the opening-victim role of Casey Becker
Highest-grossing slasher film until Halloween (2018)
Cameos: Henry Winkler (Principal Himbry), Linda Blair, Wes Craven as Fred the janitor
Won Saturn Best Horror Film, Actress (Campbell), Writing; MTV Best Movie

films.title: The Craft
films.writers: Peter Filardi and Andrew Fleming (story by Peter Filardi)
films.setting: Los Angeles; St. Benedict's Academy, a Catholic school
films.villain: Nancy Downs - power-mad coven leader; Fairuza Balk
notes: Four outcast teen witches; Sarah, newly arrived from San Francisco, completes the coven as "the fourth"
The girls worship an earth deity they call Manon
Won MTV Movie Award for Best Fight (Balk and Tunney)
Practicing Wiccan Pat Devin served as on-set advisor
Sequel The Craft: Legacy released October 28, 2020

films.title: From Dusk till Dawn
films.setting: Texas, then the Titty Twister strip bar in the Mexican desert
films.villain: Vampires of the Titty Twister, incl. Santanico Pandemonium (Salma Hayek)
notes: Concept by Robert Kurtzman of KNB EFX; the Geckos head for the hideout El Rey
Santanico Pandemonium references the 1975 film Satanico Pandemonium
Banned in Ireland in 1996; ban lifted in 2004
Followed by Texas Blood Money (1999) and prequel The Hangman's Daughter (2000)
Danny Trejo is the only actor in all three films

films.title: The Frighteners
films.setting: Fairwater (fictional town); filmed in New Zealand
films.villain: Ghost of mass murderer Johnny Bartlett (Jake Busey) posing as the Grim Reaper, aided by Patricia Bradley (Dee Wallace Stone)
notes: Bartlett was executed in 1964 for murdering 12 people at Fairwater sanatorium
Victims show glowing numbers on their foreheads before dying
Robert Zemeckis executive produced; first conceived as a Tales from the Crypt spin-off
Effects by Jackson's Weta Digital; shot entirely in New Zealand
R. Lee Ermey plays ghost drill sergeant Hiles

films.title: Thinner
films.basedOn: Thinner (1984) by Stephen King, written as Richard Bachman
films.villain: Tadzu Lempke (Michael Constantine), Romani elder who curses Billy
notes: Obese lawyer Billy Halleck kills a Romani woman and is cursed to waste away
The curse is the single word "thinner"
Stephen King cameos as Dr. Jonathan Bangor

films.title: Hellraiser: Bloodline
films.director: Kevin Yagher (credited as Alan Smithee); completed by Joe Chappelle
cast: Phillip LeMarchand / John Merchant / Dr. Paul Merchant
films.villain: Pinhead (Doug Bradley) and the demon Angelique (Valentina Vargas)
notes: Fourth Hellraiser film and the last released theatrically
Toymaker Phillip LeMarchand builds the Lament Configuration for Duc de L'Isle
Adam Scott's first major film role
Bradley is the only original cast member remaining

films.title: The Dentist
films.yearNote: Premiered June 1996 at Fantafestival; US debut on HBO Oct 18, 1996
films.genreNote: slasher; US TV premiere on HBO
films.writers: Dennis Paoli, Stuart Gordon and Charles Finch
films.villain: Dr. Alan Feinstone - obsessive-compulsive dentist who turns murderous after catching his wife cheating; Corbin Bernsen
notes: First of The Dentist series, followed by The Dentist 2
Chevy Chase and Bruce Campbell were considered for Feinstone
Ken Foree plays Detective Gibbs

films.title: Tremors 2: Aftershocks
films.yearNote: Direct-to-video, April 9, 1996
films.writers: Brent Maddock and S. S. Wilson
films.villain: Graboids and new "Shriekers"
notes: Second Tremors film; followed by Tremors 3: Back to Perfection (2001)
Earl is offered $50,000 per Graboid killed
Introduces Shriekers, hermaphrodites that multiply after eating

films.title: Tesis
films.villain: Bosco Herranz (Eduardo Noriega), snuff-film killer; Professor Castro edited the tapes
notes: Amenabar's feature debut; he also composed the score
A student writing a thesis on audiovisual violence uncovers snuff films
Won 7 Goya Awards incl. Best Film, Best New Director and Best New Actor (Fele Martinez)

films.title: Fear
films.genreNote: psychological thriller often listed with 90s horror
films.villain: David McCall - violent sociopathic boyfriend; Mark Wahlberg
notes: Producer Brian Grazer called it "Fatal Attraction for teens"
Wahlberg was nominated for the MTV Movie Award for Best Villain
Sleeper hit that made teen idols of Wahlberg and Witherspoon

films.title: Children of the Corn III: Urban Harvest
films.yearNote: Direct-to-video, Sept 12, 1995
films.basedOn: Children of the Corn by Stephen King (characters)
films.villain: Eli Porter (Daniel Cerny) and He Who Walks Behind the Rows
notes: Film debuts of Charlize Theron, Nicholas Brendon and Ivana Milicevic
Third in the series; first by Dimension Films and first direct-to-video
Brothers adopted from rural Nebraska are brought to Chicago

films.title: The Island of Dr. Moreau
films.basedOn: The Island of Doctor Moreau (1896) by H. G. Wells
films.setting: Moreau's remote island (after a Java Sea plane crash)
films.villain: Dr. Moreau (Marlon Brando) and his Beast-Folk hybrids, incl. Hyena-Swine (Daniel Rigney)
notes: Original director Richard Stanley was fired; Frankenheimer took over
Brando won the Razzie for Worst Supporting Actor
Nelson de la Rosa's Majai inspired Mini-Me in Austin Powers
Bruce Willis was originally hired before dropping out

films.title: Dracula: Dead and Loving It
films.writers: Mel Brooks, Rudy De Luca and Steve Haberman
films.basedOn: Dracula by Bram Stoker (parody)
films.villain: Count Dracula - Leslie Nielsen
notes: Mel Brooks' last film as director to date
Parodies the 1931 Dracula and Bram Stoker's Dracula (1992)
Anne Bancroft plays Madame Ouspenskaya

films.title: Scream 2
films.villain: Ghostface - revealed as film student Mickey Altieri and reporter 'Debbie Salt', really Nancy Loomis (Billy's mother); voice Roger L. Jackson
notes: 2nd Scream film; opens at a preview of 'Stab', a movie based on the Woodsboro murders
Tori Spelling, Luke Wilson, Heather Graham play Stab versions of Sidney, Billy and Casey
Script leaked online; killer-reveal pages were given to actors only on the day of shooting
$32.9M opening set the December opening-weekend record (held until 2000)
Titanic and Tomorrow Never Dies moved from Dec 12 to Dec 19, 1997 to avoid it

films.title: I Know What You Did Last Summer
films.basedOn: I Know What You Did Last Summer (1973 novel) by Lois Duncan
films.villain: The Fisherman - Ben Willis (Muse Watson), hook-wielding killer in a fisherman's slicker, the man the teens hit with their car
notes: Teens hit a man on July 4th, dump the body; a year later get the note 'I know what you did last summer!'
Ends with 'I still know' written on a shower door
No. 1 at the US box office three weekends in a row, incl. Halloween 1997
Miramax sued over ads calling it 'From the creator of Scream' and won
Sequel: I Still Know What You Did Last Summer (1998)

films.title: Anaconda
films.writers: Hans Bauer, Jim Cash, Jack Epps Jr.
films.villain: Giant green anacondas (25 ft male, 40 ft female); human villain Paraguayan snake hunter Paul Serone (Jon Voight)
notes: Documentary crew searches for the lost Shirishama tribe
Opened No. 1 with $16.6M and stayed on top a second week
6 Razzie nominations, incl. Worst New Star for 'the animatronic anaconda'
Sequel Anacondas: The Hunt for the Blood Orchid (2004); 2025 reboot with Jack Black, Paul Rudd

films.title: Event Horizon
films.director: Paul W. S. Anderson (credited as Paul Anderson)
films.setting: Derelict starship Event Horizon in orbit around Neptune, 2047
films.villain: The Event Horizon itself - its gravity drive opened a gateway to Hell; designer Dr. Weir (Sam Neill) becomes its eyeless, corrupted agent
notes: Pitched as 'a haunted house story in space'; rescue ship is the Lewis and Clark
Latin distress call 'liberate me' = 'save me'; full phrase means 'save yourself from Hell'
Ship vanished 7 years earlier on its maiden voyage to Proxima Centauri
130-min cut trimmed to 96 min; deleted footage largely lost, so no director's cut
Box-office bomb that became a cult film; shot entirely at Pinewood Studios, England

films.title: Mimic
films.basedOn: 'Mimic' (short story) by Donald A. Wollheim
films.villain: The 'Judas breed' - genetically engineered mantis-termite insects that evolve to human size and mimic people
notes: Del Toro's English-language debut
Judas breed created to kill cockroaches spreading Strickler's disease among NYC children
Del Toro clashed with the Weinsteins; his director's cut was released in 2011
Shot in Toronto; first del Toro film with Doug Jones
Sequels: Mimic 2 (2001), Mimic 3: Sentinel (2003)

films.title: Cube
films.yearNote: Premiered TIFF Sept 1997; US release Sept 1998
films.writers: Andre Bijelic, Graeme Manson, Vincenzo Natali
films.setting: A giant maze of booby-trapped cube-shaped rooms
films.villain: The Cube's deadly traps; cop Quentin (Maurice Dean Wint) turns murderous
notes: Characters named after prisons: Quentin, Holloway, Kazan, Rennes, Alderson, Leaven+Worth
Cube has 26^3 = 17,576 rooms; trap rooms marked by powers of primes
Shot in Toronto in 21 days with only one cube set built
Opening victim Alderson is sliced into cubes by a wire trap
Sequel Cube 2: Hypercube (2002), prequel Cube Zero (2004); Japanese remake 2021

films.title: Alien Resurrection
films.basedOn: Characters by Dan O'Bannon and Ronald Shusett
films.setting: Military spaceship USM Auriga, 200 years after Alien 3
films.villain: Cloned Xenomorphs, the Alien Queen and the human-Alien hybrid Newborn (creatures played by Tom Woodruff Jr.)
notes: 4th Alien film; Ripley 8 is a clone carrying Alien Queen DNA (acid blood, extra strength)
Call (Winona Ryder) is revealed to be a synthetic 'Auton'
Weaver made the backward basketball shot herself on the first take
Mercenaries' ship is the Betty; the Auriga crashes into Earth
Ripley's last line: 'I'm a stranger here myself.'

films.title: The Devil's Advocate
films.basedOn: The Devil's Advocate (1990 novel) by Andrew Neiderman
films.setting: New York City law firm (Kevin starts in Gainesville, Florida)
films.villain: John Milton (Al Pacino), head of the law firm, revealed as Satan and Kevin's father
notes: Final line: 'Vanity - definitely my favorite sin.'
Won the Saturn Award for Best Horror Film
Kevin is an undefeated Florida lawyer; Christabella is his half-sister
Reeves chose it over Speed 2 and took a pay cut so producers could pay Pacino
Devil named after Paradise Lost poet John Milton

films.title: The Relic
films.writers: Amy Holden Jones, John Raffo, Rick Jaffa & Amanda Silver
films.basedOn: Relic (1995 novel) by Douglas Preston and Lincoln Child
films.setting: Field Museum of Natural History, Chicago
films.villain: The Kothoga - South American lizard-like beast, revealed as mutated anthropologist John Whitney; creature effects by Stan Winston
notes: Kothoga kills to eat human hypothalami
Shot at the real Field Museum after New York's natural history museum declined
Omits the novel's FBI agent Pendergast
Released Jan 10, 1997 and opened No. 1, but flopped
Final film of actress Audra Lindley

films.title: An American Werewolf in Paris
films.writers: Tim Burns, Tom Stern, Anthony Waller
films.basedOn: Characters by John Landis
films.villain: Claude (Pierre Cosso), leader of a werewolf society luring victims to the Club de la Lune
notes: Sequel to An American Werewolf in London (1981)
Andy saves Serafine during a bungee jump off the Eiffel Tower
Cure: eat the heart of the werewolf that bit you
Ends with a wedding atop the Statue of Liberty
CGI transformations replaced the original's Rick Baker makeup; Landis called it 'lousy'

films.title: Wishmaster
films.villain: The Djinn (Andrew Divoff), evil wish-twisting genie freed from a fire opal
notes: Executive produced by Wes Craven ('Wes Craven presents')
Cameos by horror icons Englund, Hodder, Todd, Ted Raimi, Reggie Bannister; Angus Scrimm narrates
Djinn must grant his releaser three wishes to free his race
Verne Troyer plays the small Djinn when first released
Sequels: Wishmaster 2: Evil Never Dies (1999) and two more

films.title: Funny Games
films.genreNote: Austrian psychological thriller often listed as horror; German-language
films.villain: Paul (Arno Frisch) and Peter (Frank Giering), polite young men who hold the family hostage
notes: Home invasion begins with a request to borrow eggs
Paul breaks the fourth wall and rewinds the film with a remote
Premiered at Cannes 1997; about a third of the audience walked out
Haneke remade it shot-for-shot in the US in 2007 (Naomi Watts, Tim Roth)

films.title: The Shining
films.genreNote: ABC TV miniseries (3 parts), aired Apr 27-May 1, 1997
films.basedOn: The Shining (1977 novel) by Stephen King
films.villain: The Overlook Hotel's evil spirits, incl. former caretaker Delbert Grady and founder Horace Derwent
notes: Made because King disliked Kubrick's 1980 film
Filmed at the Stanley Hotel, Estes Park, Colorado - King's inspiration
Stephen King cameos as orchestra conductor Gage Creed; Sam Raimi as gas station attendant
Won 2 Primetime Emmys (makeup; sound editing)
Ghost of Room 217 played by Cynthia Garris, the director's wife

films.title: Leprechaun 4: In Space
films.yearNote: First released Russia Oct 1996; US direct-to-video Feb 25, 1997
films.basedOn: Characters by Mark Jones
films.setting: A remote planet and a space marine ship, 2096
films.villain: The Leprechaun (Warwick Davis), aiming to wed alien Princess Zarina and become king
notes: 4th Leprechaun film; followed by Leprechaun in the Hood (2000)
Leprechaun is turned giant by a growth ray and blown out an airlock
Self-destruct password is 'Wizard'

films.title: Nightwatch
films.yearNote: Festival premiere 1997; US theatrical release April 1998
films.basedOn: Nightwatch (Nattevagten, 1994 Danish film) by Ole Bornedal
films.villain: Necrophiliac serial killer of prostitutes who removes victims' eyes - revealed as Inspector Thomas Cray (Nick Nolte)
notes: Remake of the 1994 Danish film by the same director
Ewan McGregor's first American film; he plays a law student and morgue night watchman
Josh Brolin plays Martin's friend James; John C. Reilly appears uncredited

films.title: Campfire Tales
films.yearNote: UK video May 1997; US video release Sept 1998
films.director: Matt Cooper, Martin Kunert, David Semel
films.writers: Martin Kunert, Eric Manes, Matt Cooper
films.setting: Campfire in the woods after a car crash (anthology of urban legends)
films.villain: Anthology: hook-handed madman, unseen creatures, online predator ('People Can Lick Too'), ghostly axe-wielding father
notes: Segments: The Hook, The Honeymoon, People Can Lick Too, The Locket
Framing twist: the storytellers died in their car crash
Film debut of Jacinda Barrett; Christine Taylor also stars
Bollywood's Darna Mana Hai (2003) was loosely based on it

films.title: Jack Frost
films.villain: Jack Frost (Scott MacDonald), serial killer fused with snow by genetic chemicals into a killer snowman
notes: Film debut of Shannon Elizabeth
Jack killed 38 people in 11 states; finally melted with antifreeze
Not the 1998 Michael Keaton family film of the same name
Sequel: Jack Frost 2: Revenge of the Mutant Killer Snowman (2000)

films.title: The Night Flier
films.yearNote: Italy May 1997; US HBO premiere Nov 1997; US theatrical Feb 1998
films.basedOn: The Night Flier (1988 short story) by Stephen King
films.distributor: New Line Cinema (US theatrical); HBO (TV premiere)
films.setting: Rural US airfields; climax at Wilmington airfield
films.villain: Dwight Renfield (Michael H. Moss), vampire pilot of a black Cessna Skymaster killing at airfields
notes: Dees' motto: 'Never believe what you publish and never publish what you believe.'
Dees is a tabloid reporter for Inside View
Vampire's name honors Dwight Frye, Renfield in Dracula (1931)
Film debut of Julie Entwisle

films.title: Cure
films.villain: Kunihiko Mamiya (Masato Hagiwara), amnesiac drifter who hypnotizes strangers into murder
notes: Victims have a large 'X' carved into the neck or chest
Original title Evangelist; changed after the Aum Shinrikyo sarin attack
Premiered at Tokyo International Film Festival, Nov 6, 1997
Seen as a forerunner of the J-horror wave (Ring, Ju-On)

films.title: Perfect Blue
films.yearNote: Premiered Fantasia festival Aug 1997; Japan release Feb 1998
films.genreNote: Japanese animated psychological thriller often listed as horror
films.basedOn: Perfect Blue: Complete Metamorphosis (novel) by Yoshikazu Takeuchi
films.setting: Japan's J-pop idol and TV-drama world
films.villain: Mima's manager Rumi Hidaka, posing as 'the real Mima' and committing the murders; stalker Me-Mania
notes: Satoshi Kon's first film; animated by Madhouse
Mima leaves idol group CHAM! to become an actress
Website 'Mima's Room' posts her private diary
Aronofsky's Requiem for a Dream remakes its bathtub scene

films.title: Halloween H20: 20 Years Later
films.writers: Robert Zappia and Matt Greenberg (screenplay); story by Robert Zappia
films.basedOn: Characters created by John Carpenter and Debra Hill
films.setting: Hillcrest Academy boarding school, Summer Glen, California
films.villain: Michael Myers (Chris Durand), Laurie's brother; Laurie beheads him with an axe at the end
notes: 7th Halloween film; direct sequel to Halloween (1978) and Halloween II (1981), ignoring parts 4-6
Josh Hartnett's film debut, as Laurie's son John
Janet Leigh (Curtis's real-life mother, star of Psycho) drives the same car model she drove in Psycho
Highest-grossing Halloween film until Halloween (2018); opened with $16.2M
Scream writer Kevin Williamson did uncredited rewrites; Dr. Loomis voice is sound-alike Tom Kane

films.title: Bride of Chucky
films.basedOn: Characters created by Don Mancini (Child's Play)
films.setting: Lockport, New York, then a road trip to Hackensack, New Jersey
films.villain: Chucky (voice Brad Dourif) and his ex-girlfriend Tiffany Valentine (Jennifer Tilly), whose soul Chucky puts into a bride doll
notes: 4th Child's Play film; first without Andy Barclay; working title Child's Play 4: The Return of Chucky
Tiffany idea came from producer David Kirschner after seeing Bride of Frankenstein
The dolls seek the Heart of Damballa amulet, buried with Chucky's human body
Ends with Tiffany giving birth to a doll baby; sequel Seed of Chucky (2004)
Highest-grossing Chucky film; shot in and around Toronto

films.title: Urban Legend
films.setting: Pendleton University, a fictional New England college
films.villain: Axe-wielding killer in a hooded parka - revealed as Brenda Bates (Rebecca Gayheart), avenging her fiance David Evans
notes: Murders copy urban legends: killer in the backseat, Pop Rocks and soda, The Hook, the microwaved dog
Roommate's death note: Aren't you glad you didn't turn on the light?
Robert Englund (Freddy Krueger) plays a folklore professor; Danielle Harris plays roommate Tosh
Brad Dourif has an uncredited cameo as the gas station attendant in the opening
University of Toronto stood in for Pendleton; sequels Final Cut (2000) and Bloody Mary (2005)

films.title: The Faculty
films.writers: Kevin Williamson (screenplay); story by David Wechter and Bruce Kimmel
films.villain: Parasitic aliens taking over the teachers; the alien queen is new student Marybeth Hutchinson (Laura Harris)
notes: Jordana Brewster's film debut
Aliens die from Zeke's homemade 'drug' - actually powdered caffeine, which dehydrates them
Also features Salma Hayek (Nurse Harper), Usher (Gabe), Piper Laurie and Bebe Neuwirth
Released Christmas Day 1998; shot in Austin and other Texas towns
1990 spec script was bought by Miramax only after the success of Scream

films.title: I Still Know What You Did Last Summer
films.basedOn: Characters by Lois Duncan
films.setting: Tower Bay resort island in the Bahamas (opens in Boston)
films.villain: Ben Willis, the hook-wielding Fisherman (Muse Watson), helped by his son Will Benson (Matthew Settle)
notes: 2nd film in the I Know What You Did Last Summer series; set one year after the first
Trip 'won' by answering capital of Brazil as Rio de Janeiro - a wrong answer exposing the setup
Jack Black has an uncredited role as pool boy Titus Telesco
Hewitt sings 'How Do I Deal' on the soundtrack
Beat Species II for Worst Sequel at the 1998 Stinkers Bad Movie Awards

films.title: Blade
films.basedOn: Marvel Comics character Blade, created by Marv Wolfman and Gene Colan
films.setting: Unnamed American city (shot in Los Angeles)
films.villain: Deacon Frost (Stephen Dorff), upstart vampire who becomes the blood god La Magra; killed with an EDTA overdose
notes: Blade is the 'Daywalker' - half-vampire with their strengths but none of their weaknesses
Blade first appeared in 1973 in Marvel's The Tomb of Dracula
Opened #1, ending Saving Private Ryan's run on top; called Marvel's first successful film
Stephen Dorff won the MTV Movie Award for Best Villain
Sequels Blade II (2002) and Blade: Trinity (2004); Snipes returned in Deadpool & Wolverine (2024)

films.title: Ringu
films.yearNote: Japan release Jan 31, 1998; US home video Mar 2003 as Ringu
films.basedOn: Ring (1991 novel) by Koji Suzuki
films.setting: Japan - an Izu resort cabin and Oshima Island
films.villain: Sadako Yamamura (Rie Ino), psychic girl thrown down a well by Dr. Ikuma; her vengeful spirit curses a videotape
notes: Cursed videotape kills viewers seven days after watching, announced by a phone call
Only escape: copy the tape and show it to someone else within seven days
Shot back-to-back with sequel Spiral; both opened in Japan the same day
Became Japan's highest-grossing horror film on release; budget about $1.5M
Remade as The Ring Virus (Korea, 1999) and The Ring (US, 2002); direct sequel Ring 2 (1999)

films.title: Psycho (1998)
films.basedOn: Psycho (1959 novel) by Robert Bloch
films.setting: Phoenix, Arizona and the Bates Motel near Fairvale, California
films.villain: Norman Bates (Vince Vaughn) in his 'Mother' persona; Norma Bates voiced by Rose Marie (uncredited)
notes: Near shot-for-shot color remake of Hitchcock's 1960 film, set in 1998
Stolen money raised from $40,000 to $400,000
Won Razzies for Worst Remake or Sequel (three-way tie) and Worst Director
Bernard Herrmann's score rearranged by Danny Elfman and Steve Bartek
Nicole Kidman was first cast as Marion; Rick Baker designed the Mother dummy

films.title: Disturbing Behavior
films.setting: Cradle Bay, an island town in Puget Sound, Washington
films.villain: School psychologist Dr. Edgar Caldicott (Bruce Greenwood), who microchips teens into the clean-cut 'Blue Ribbons'
notes: Blue Ribbons have brain chips; the whine of a rat-repelling device sends them into a frenzy
Director David Nutter came from The X-Files; film nods to The Stepford Wives
MGM cut 31 minutes, leaving an 84-minute theatrical version
Shot in the Vancouver area

films.title: Phantoms
films.basedOn: Phantoms (1983 novel) by Dean Koontz
films.villain: The Ancient Enemy - shapeshifting amoeba-like entity that absorbs and mimics victims; killed with oil-eating bacteria
notes: Dean Koontz adapted his own novel
Flyte writes the book The Ancient Enemy; the entity wiped out the Maya and Roanoke colonists
Filmed in Georgetown, Colorado
Affleck's teeth look whiter in reshoots made after Armageddon
Referenced in Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back (2001)

films.title: Vampires
films.basedOn: Vampire$ (novel) by John Steakley
films.villain: Jan Valek (Thomas Ian Griffith), the first vampire, seeking the Black Cross of Beziers; aided by Cardinal Alba (Maximilian Schell)
notes: Jack Crow leads a Vatican-sponsored team of vampire slayers
Carpenter also composed the score
James Woods won the Saturn for Best Actor; film had the most wins (3) at the 25th Saturns
Opened #1 ahead of Pleasantville; Carpenter's only financial success of the 1990s
Alec Baldwin dropped out and recommended his brother Daniel

films.title: Fallen
films.villain: Azazel, a fallen angel that jumps between hosts by touch; first seen in executed killer Edgar Reese (Elias Koteas)
notes: Possessed hosts sing the Rolling Stones' 'Time Is on My Side'
Reese speaks Syriac Aramaic just before his execution
Twist: Azazel survives in a cat; credits play 'Sympathy for the Devil'
James Gandolfini plays Detective Lou

films.title: Strangeland
films.villain: Captain Howdy / Carlton Hendricks (Dee Snider), body-modification sadist who lures teens through chat rooms
notes: Written by Twisted Sister singer Dee Snider, based on the band's song 'Horror-Teria'
Robert Englund plays vigilante Jackson Roth
Victims have their mouths stitched shut

films.title: Children of the Corn V: Fields of Terror
films.yearNote: Direct-to-video release, June 21, 1998
films.basedOn: Children of the Corn (short story) by Stephen King
films.setting: Divinity Falls, a rural town in middle America
films.villain: He Who Walks Behind the Rows, possessing cult leader Ezekiel (Adam Wylie); cult patriarch Luke Enright (David Carradine)
notes: 5th Children of the Corn film
Cult members sacrifice themselves by leaping into a flaming corn silo
David Carradine plays Luke; Kane Hodder cameos as a bartender
Working title Fields of Screams was changed to avoid confusion with Scream

films.title: Gods and Monsters
films.yearNote: Sundance premiere Jan 1998; US release Nov 4, 1998
films.genreNote: period drama about Frankenstein director James Whale; horror-adjacent
films.basedOn: Father of Frankenstein (1995 novel) by Christopher Bram
films.setting: 1950s, home of retired director James Whale
notes: Won the Oscar for Best Adapted Screenplay; McKellen and Redgrave were nominated
Title from Dr. Pretorius's toast: 'To a new world of gods and monsters!'
Lynn Redgrave won the Golden Globe for Best Supporting Actress
Clive Barker was executive producer
Gardener Clayton Boone is a fictional character invented for the novel

films.title: Apt Pupil
films.basedOn: Apt Pupil (1982 novella in Different Seasons) by Stephen King
films.villain: Kurt Dussander (Ian McKellen), fugitive Nazi death camp commandant living as Arthur Denker
notes: Won the Saturn Award for Best Horror Film of 1998; McKellen won Saturn Best Supporting Actor
Stephen King optioned the rights to Singer for $1
A 1987 version with Nicol Williamson and Rick Schroder was abandoned after ten weeks
Filmed in Altadena, California; John Ottman both edited and scored
Novella ends with Todd's shooting spree; film changes the ending

films.title: Deep Rising
films.setting: Luxury cruise ship Argonautica, South China Sea
films.villain: The Octalus, a giant tentacled deep-sea monster; ship owner Simon Canton (Anthony Heald) is the human saboteur
notes: Working title Tentacle; ends with Finnegan's line 'Now what?'
Effects by ILM; creature makeup by Rob Bottin
Harrison Ford turned down Finnegan; Claire Forlani left the Trillian role after three days

films.title: Species II
films.basedOn: Characters by Dennis Feldman (Species, 1995)
films.setting: Earth after the first manned mission to Mars
films.villain: Astronaut Patrick Ross (Justin Lazard), infected with alien DNA on a Mars mission
notes: Sequel to Species (1995); Henstridge plays Eve, a more docile clone of Sil
Alien designs had input from H. R. Giger
Astronaut Dennis Gamble's sickle cell trait is used to kill Ross
Peter Boyle has an uncredited role as Dr. Herman Cromwell

films.title: The Blair Witch Project
films.setting: Black Hills Forest near Burkittsville, Maryland (October 1994)
films.villain: The unseen Blair Witch (legend of Elly Kedward, banished for witchcraft in 1785); legend also features 1940s child-killer Rustin Parr
notes: Found-footage film shot by the three actors themselves in 8 days (Oct 1997); dialogue improvised from a 35-page outline
Artisan bought it for $1.1M after its midnight Sundance premiere (Jan 1999)
Marketed as real via an early Internet campaign; actors billed as missing or presumed dead
Ends with Mike standing in a basement corner, echoing Rustin Parr's murders
Heather Donahue won the Razzie for Worst Actress; film won Independent Spirit John Cassavetes Award

films.title: The Sixth Sense
films.genreNote: supernatural psychological thriller often listed as horror
films.villain: No single villain; ex-patient Vincent Grey (Donnie Wahlberg) shoots Malcolm; Kyra's mother poisoned Kyra
notes: Twist: child psychologist Malcolm has been dead since Vincent shot him
Famous line: 'I see dead people' (AFI movie quotes list No. 44)
6 Oscar nominations incl. Best Picture, Osment and Collette; won none
Record August opening ($26.6M) until Rush Hour 2 (2001); 5 weekends at No. 1
Won Saturn Award for Best Horror Film; red color marks things touched by the other world

films.title: The Mummy
films.genreNote: action-adventure horror; loose remake of the 1932 Universal film
films.writers: Stephen Sommers (screenplay); story by Stephen Sommers, Lloyd Fonvielle, Kevin Jarre
films.basedOn: The Mummy (1932 film) by John L. Balderston, Nina Wilcox Putnam, Richard Schayer
films.setting: Cairo and Hamunaptra (City of the Dead), Egypt, 1926
films.villain: Imhotep (Arnold Vosloo), high priest cursed and buried alive with flesh-eating scarabs for loving Anck-su-namun
notes: Evelyn reads the Book of the Dead to wake Imhotep; the golden Book of Amun-Ra makes him mortal
Opened No. 1 with $43M, the highest non-holiday May opening at the time
Oscar nominee for Best Sound; won Saturn Award for Best Make-up
Shot in Marrakesh and the Sahara near Erfoud, Morocco; Hamunaptra built at Gara Medouar
Sequels: The Mummy Returns (2001), Tomb of the Dragon Emperor (2008); spinoff The Scorpion King (2002)

films.title: Sleepy Hollow
films.writers: Andrew Kevin Walker (screenplay); story by Kevin Yagher and Andrew Kevin Walker
films.basedOn: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow (1820 short story) by Washington Irving
cast: Lady Mary Van Tassel / the Crone
films.villain: Headless Horseman (Hessian Horseman, Christopher Walken), controlled by Lady Mary Van Tassel (Miranda Richardson) via his stolen skull
notes: Won Oscar for Best Art Direction (Rick Heinrichs, Peter Young); nominated for Cinematography and Costume Design
Ichabod is a NYC constable using forensic science, not Irving's schoolmaster
Depp's third Burton film after Edward Scissorhands and Ed Wood
Saturn Awards: Christina Ricci Best Actress; Danny Elfman Best Music
Martin Landau has an uncredited cameo as Peter Van Garrett

films.title: The Haunting
films.basedOn: The Haunting of Hill House (1959 novel) by Shirley Jackson
films.setting: Hill House, the Berkshires, western Massachusetts
films.villain: Ghost of Hugh Crain (Charles Gunning), 19th-century textile tycoon who killed child laborers
notes: Second film of the novel, after Robert Wise's The Haunting (1963)
Marrow's 'insomnia study' is secretly a study of fear
Hill House exterior was Harlaxton Manor, Lincolnshire, England
Began as a Spielberg-Stephen King project; King's script became Rose Red (2002)
Opened No. 1 ($33.4M); 5 Razzie nominations incl. Worst Picture

films.title: House on Haunted Hill
films.writers: Dick Beebe (screenplay); story by Robb White
films.basedOn: House on Haunted Hill (1959 William Castle film written by Robb White)
films.setting: Vannacutt Psychiatric Institute for the Criminally Insane, Los Angeles
films.villain: Ghost of Dr. Richard B. Vannacutt (Jeffrey Combs) and an amorphous mass of the asylum's spirits; Evelyn and Dr. Blackburn plot murder
notes: Amusement park mogul Price offers $1 million to each guest who survives the night
First film from Dark Castle Entertainment (Joel Silver, Robert Zemeckis)
Price's name honors Vincent Price, star of the 1959 original
Opened No. 1 on Halloween weekend 1999; theaters gave out prize scratchcards
Sequel: Return to House on Haunted Hill (2007, direct-to-DVD)

films.title: Deep Blue Sea
films.writers: Duncan Kennedy, Donna Powers, Wayne Powers
films.setting: Remote underwater shark research facility at sea
films.villain: Genetically engineered mako sharks with enlarged, smarter brains
notes: Sharks engineered so brain protein could be harvested for an Alzheimer's cure
Samuel L. Jackson's character is eaten mid-speech about group unity
Shot at Fox Baja Studios, Rosarito, in water tanks built for Titanic
LL Cool J contributed 'Deepest Bluest (Shark's Fin)'; Preacher's parrot is eaten
Original ending had Susan survive; reshot after test audiences objected

films.title: Lake Placid
films.villain: Giant 32-ft saltwater crocodile (one of a mating pair)
notes: Written by TV writer David E. Kelley (Ally McBeal, The Practice)
Betty White's widow Mrs. Bickerman feeds the crocodile cows; it ate her husband
Crocodile built by Stan Winston Studios
British Columbia lakes stood in for Black Lake
First of a series; Lake Placid 2 (2007) began the TV sequels

films.title: Idle Hands
films.villain: Stoner Anton's possessed right hand (The Hand, Christopher Hart), which keeps killing after he cuts it off
notes: Title from the saying 'idle hands are the devil's playthings'
Murdered friends Mick and Pnub return as zombies
