The Offspring cameo; the Hand scalps singer Dexter Holland at the school dance
Released the month of the Columbine shooting; Sen. Joe Lieberman criticized it
Druid priestess Debi LeCure hunts the evil spirit

films.title: Stir of Echoes
films.basedOn: A Stir of Echoes (1958 novel) by Richard Matheson
films.villain: Neighbors' sons Adam McCarthy and Kurt Damon, who killed Samantha; fathers Frank McCarthy and Harry Damon covered it up
notes: Phone lineman Tom gets visions after sister-in-law Lisa hypnotizes him at a party
Samantha's ghost tells Tom to 'dig'; her body is hidden behind a basement wall
Ghost filmed at six frames per second for otherworldly motion
Released weeks after The Sixth Sense and overshadowed by it
TV sequel: Stir of Echoes: The Homecoming (2007, Sci Fi Channel)

films.title: Stigmata
films.writers: Tom Lazarus and Rick Ramage (screenplay); story by Tom Lazarus
films.setting: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania (prologue in Belo Quinto, Brazil)
films.villain: Cardinal Daniel Houseman (Jonathan Pryce), suppressing a lost gospel; Frankie is possessed by dead priest Paulo Alameida's spirit
notes: Atheist hairdresser gets the stigmata after receiving a dead priest's rosary
Score by Billy Corgan with Mike Garson and Elia Cmiral
Opened No. 1 ($18.3M), first film in five weekends to top The Sixth Sense
Closing text refers to the Gospel of Thomas
Saturn Award nominee for Best Horror Film

films.title: End of Days
films.villain: Satan (Gabriel Byrne), possessing an investment banker
notes: Satan must impregnate Christine before midnight Dec 31, 1999 to sire the Antichrist
Jericho Cane role was written for Tom Cruise
Jericho dies impaled on a sword held by a statue of Archangel Michael
Soundtrack had Guns N' Roses' 'Oh My God', first song by the new lineup
Schwarzenegger was paid $25M; Razzie noms for him, Byrne and Hyams

films.title: The Ninth Gate
films.yearNote: Premiered San Sebastian, Spain Aug 25, 1999; US release Mar 10, 2000
films.genreNote: supernatural mystery thriller often listed as horror
films.writers: John Brownjohn, Enrique Urbizu, Roman Polanski
films.basedOn: The Club Dumas (1993 novel) by Arturo Perez-Reverte
films.setting: New York City and Europe (Toledo, Sintra, Paris)
films.villain: Book collector Boris Balkan (Frank Langella), trying to summon the Devil; Liana Telfer's Satanic cult
notes: Rare-book dealer Corso authenticates 'The Nine Gates of the Kingdom of Shadows' by Aristide de Torchia
Authentic engravings are signed 'LCF' (Lucifer); only three copies survived
Depp met longtime partner Vanessa Paradis during filming
Score by Wojciech Kilar
Polanski's adaptation drops the novel's Three Musketeers subplot

films.title: Ravenous
films.villain: F.W. Colqhoun / Colonel Ives (Robert Carlyle), cannibal empowered by eating human flesh per the Wendigo myth
notes: Score by Michael Nyman and Blur's Damon Albarn
Director Milcho Manchevski was fired; Antonia Bird took over on Carlyle's suggestion
Inspired by the Donner Party and 'Colorado Cannibal' Alfred Packer
Shot in Slovakia's Tatra Mountains and Durango, Mexico

films.title: Audition
films.yearNote: Premiered Vancouver IFF Oct 2, 1999; Japan release Mar 3, 2000; US release Aug 2001
films.basedOn: Audition (1997 novel) by Ryu Murakami
films.villain: Asami Yamazaki (Eihi Shiina), ex-ballerina who tortures with acupuncture needles and a wire saw
notes: Widower stages a fake film casting call to find a new wife
Asami's chant 'kiri kiri kiri' was added during filming
Former model Eihi Shiina's acting debut
Won the FIPRESCI Prize at the 2000 Rotterdam film festival
Produced by Omega Project, the company behind Ring (1998)

films.title: The Rage: Carrie 2
films.basedOn: Characters from Carrie (1974 novel) by Stephen King; sequel to Carrie (1976 film)
films.setting: Small Maine town with the ruins of Carrie White's high school
films.villain: Football players scoring sexual conquests (Mark Bing, Eric Stark); Rachel's telekinetic party massacre
notes: Rachel is Carrie White's half-sister (same father, Ralph White)
Emily Bergl's film debut
Amy Irving reprises Sue Snell, who is killed by a fire poker
Sissy Spacek appears as Carrie only via archival footage
Began as an unrelated script, The Curse; Katt Shea replaced director Robert Mandel

films.title: Candyman: Day of the Dead
films.basedOn: Characters created by Clive Barker
films.setting: Los Angeles, around the Day of the Dead
films.villain: Candyman / Daniel Robitaille (Tony Todd), hook-handed spirit summoned by saying his name five times in a mirror
notes: Third Candyman film; direct sequel to Candyman: Farewell to the Flesh (1995)
Caroline is Annie Tarrant's daughter and Candyman's descendant
Released direct-to-video July 9, 1999; shot in 18 days for about $1M
Philip Glass's earlier Candyman music could not be used; new score by Adam Gorgoni

films.title: Bats
films.villain: Genetically mutated, omnivorous killer bats created by Dr. Alexander McCabe (Bob Gunton)
notes: First film released by Destination Films
Bats are frozen in their abandoned-mine roost with an industrial coolant
TV sequel: Bats: Human Harvest (2007, Sci-Fi Channel)

films.title: The Astronaut's Wife
films.genreNote: sci-fi thriller often listed as horror
films.setting: New York City (after a NASA space mission)
films.villain: Alien entity that possessed astronaut Spencer Armacost (Johnny Depp) during a spacewalk
notes: Rand Ravich's feature directorial debut
Dylan and Cole Sprouse play Jillian's alien-fathered twins
Critics compared it to Rosemary's Baby

films.title: Virus
films.basedOn: Virus (Dark Horse comic) by Chuck Pfarrer
films.setting: Russian research ship Akademik Vladislav Volkov, South Pacific, during a typhoon
films.villain: Alien electrical intelligence from space station Mir that turns the crew into cyborgs
notes: Directed by visual effects artist John Bruno
The alien calls humanity a 'virus' to use as spare parts
Jamie Lee Curtis has called it one of the worst films she made

facts.text: The Silence of the Lambs (1991) won the Big Five at the 64th Academy Awards (Mar 30, 1992): Picture, Director (Jonathan Demme), Actor (Anthony Hopkins), Actress (Jodie Foster), Adapted Screenplay (Ted Tally).
Kathy Bates won Best Actress as Annie Wilkes in Misery (1990) at the 63rd Academy Awards (Mar 25, 1991) - the film's only nomination. She also won the Golden Globe for Best Actress - Drama.
Bram Stoker's Dracula (1992) won 3 of 4 Oscars at the 65th Academy Awards (1993): Costume Design (Eiko Ishioka), Makeup (Greg Cannom et al.), Sound Effects Editing; lost Art Direction.
Sleepy Hollow (1999) won Best Art Direction (Rick Heinrichs, Peter Young) at the 72nd Academy Awards (Mar 26, 2000); also nominated for Cinematography and Costume Design (Colleen Atwood).
The Sixth Sense (1999) got 6 Oscar nominations, 0 wins: Picture; Director and Original Screenplay (M. Night Shyamalan); Supp. Actor (Haley Joel Osment); Supp. Actress (Toni Collette); Film Editing.
The Sixth Sense (1999) became the highest-grossing horror film ever, passing The Exorcist, and held the record until It (2017), which reached about $704M.
Scream grossed $173M worldwide ($103M US). It was the highest-grossing slasher film until Halloween (2018), and Miramax's second $100M US film after Pulp Fiction.
The Blair Witch Project grossed $248.6M worldwide ($140.5M US/Canada) after a tiny budget; 10th-highest-grossing US film of 1999.
Halloween H20 was the highest-grossing Halloween film until Halloween (2018); Bride of Chucky is the highest-grossing Chucky film.
Leonardo DiCaprio made his film debut as Josh in Critters 3 (1991).
Jennifer Aniston's first major film role was Tory Redding in Leprechaun (1993); she earlier had an uncredited bit in Mac and Me (1988).
Paul Rudd made his feature film debut in Halloween: The Curse of Michael Myers (credited as Paul Stephen Rudd), playing Tommy Doyle.
Josh Hartnett made his film debut in Halloween H20 and also starred in The Faculty the same year.
Drew Barrymore was first cast as Sidney in Scream but asked for the smaller role of Casey Becker, who dies in the opening.
Charlize Theron made her film debut in an uncredited, non-speaking role in Children of the Corn III: Urban Harvest (1995).
Brandon Lee was killed on The Crow set on Mar 31, 1993 (EUE Screen Gems, Wilmington, NC) by a bullet lodged in a prop .44 revolver (squib load).
Candyman used over 200,000 real honeybees; Tony Todd negotiated a $1,000 bonus per sting and was stung 23 times.
The Ghostface mask in Scream was based on Fun World's 1991 'Peanut-Eyed Ghost' costume design.
'I see dead people.' - Cole Sear (Haley Joel Osment), The Sixth Sense; No. 44 on AFI's 100 movie quotes.
The Silence of the Lambs: 'I ate his liver with some fava beans and a nice Chianti' (AFI No. 21); Lecter's closing line is about 'having an old friend for dinner.'
Army of Darkness: Ash says 'Hail to the king, baby'; the Necronomicon words are 'Klaatu barada nikto'.
Hideo Nakata's Ring (1998, Japan) launched the J-horror boom and was remade in English as The Ring (2002).
Braindead (1992), Peter Jackson's New Zealand zombie splatter comedy set in Wellington, was released in the US as Dead Alive.
